scope: Discovery-centered union. Scientific credit pools are provisional and can exceed three; the agents must select a coherent award of no more than three people in total. No shortlist ranking, probabilities or nominator counts are implied.
limitations: Recipient pools are evidence-informed starting points, not exhaustive priority judgments. Agents may propose additional names with sources.

Living-status review is targeted, not a comprehensive current registry audit for every retained person. Known deceased pioneers are historical credit only; recheck shortlisted recipients before final selection.
Membership in a previous prize-winning team or being a previous Nobel laureate does not automatically bar a distinct achievement; already rewarded achievements require explicit overlap review.
The broad tau/alpha-synuclein entry contains separable discoveries; agents should narrow its final citation and recipients if selected.
Committee identity and coauthorship flags require handling before simulation dispatch; they are not evidence of actual institutional disqualification.

candidates.discovery: A bispecific antibody that substitutes for factor VIII activity in hemophilia A
candidates.scientific_basis: Emicizumab bridges coagulation factors IX and X to compensate for deficient factor VIII activity.
candidates.rationale: A specific engineering invention with a clear clinical mechanism and substantial treatment benefit.
candidates.main_reservation: Could be viewed as a powerful disease-specific invention rather than a broad physiological discovery.
candidates.attribution_note: The 2026 Lasker supports this three-person pool; the citation should focus on factor-mimetic bispecific engineering rather than all antibody therapeutics.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids for studying tissue biology and disease
candidates.scientific_basis: Single intestinal stem cells can generate self-organizing organoids, enabling long-term culture of tissue-like structures.
candidates.rationale: Changed experimental access to normal and diseased human tissues through a concrete biological discovery and culture method.
candidates.main_reservation: Clinical impact and physiological completeness vary; adult stem-cell organoids should be distinguished from pluripotent stem-cell organoids.
candidates.attribution_note: This narrow scope supports Clevers and Sato; a broader organoid citation would require additional pioneers and separate attribution research.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Toshiro Sato for the original adult intestinal organoid experiment, alongside Hans Clevers; stem-cell identification and culture invention are distinguished.

candidates.discovery: AMP-activated protein kinase as a sensor and regulator of cellular energy balance
candidates.scientific_basis: AMPK responds to cellular nucleotide/energy status and coordinates ATP-producing and ATP-consuming processes.
candidates.rationale: A pervasive energy-sensing mechanism in cell physiology.
candidates.main_reservation: A broad discovery with significant collaborators; metformin action cannot be treated as exclusively AMPK-dependent.
candidates.attribution_note: Hardie’s laboratory defined the AMPK cascade. David Carling, Bruce Kemp and other mechanistic contributors require consideration if agents broaden the recipient pool; the retained singleton does not imply exclusive authorship.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing to treat spinal muscular atrophy
candidates.scientific_basis: An antisense oligonucleotide redirects SMN2 splicing to increase functional survival motor neuron protein.
candidates.rationale: A precise RNA mechanism translated into an effective treatment for a devastating inherited disease.
candidates.main_reservation: The citation should recognize the SMA splicing intervention rather than all antisense therapeutics.
candidates.attribution_note: Krainer contributed splicing mechanism/design and Bennett antisense therapeutic development. The pool does not claim exclusive credit for the entire antisense field or clinical trial program.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: APP mutations and the amyloid-cascade model of Alzheimer’s disease
candidates.scientific_basis: Inherited APP mutations linked amyloid biology directly to familial Alzheimer’s disease and helped motivate the amyloid-cascade model.
candidates.rationale: A causally anchored genetic insight that directed decades of disease research.
candidates.main_reservation: The hypothesis is not a complete explanation of sporadic Alzheimer’s disease, and evidence for therapy does not identify its inventors.
candidates.attribution_note: Goate was lead geneticist/first author of the APP mutation work in Hardy’s program and is restored to the pool. Hardy helped formulate the cascade model. Dennis Selkoe and other biochemical/genetic pioneers merit consideration if the agents broaden beyond APP-linked causality.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: BCL-2-mediated cell survival, apoptosis control, and the basis of targeted cancer therapy
candidates.scientific_basis: BCL-2 oncogenic activity was shown to inhibit cell death rather than simply stimulate division, opening a therapeutic survival pathway.
candidates.rationale: A mechanistic discovery with subsequent effective cancer therapy.
candidates.main_reservation: A clinical drug-invention citation would need review of medicinal chemistry and clinical teams beyond this biology pool.
candidates.attribution_note: Vaux, Cory and Adams authored the 1988 survival paper; Adams was missing from Claude’s pool and is restored. Strasser established key in-vivo consequences and BCL-2-family functions. This is not a claim that these four alone invented venetoclax.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: BCL11A regulation of fetal hemoglobin and its therapeutic reactivation in hemoglobin disorders
candidates.scientific_basis: Human genetic associations, repressor experiments and erythroid-enhancer targeting linked BCL11A to fetal hemoglobin silencing and therapeutic reactivation.
candidates.rationale: A strong chain from human genetics to a defined molecular intervention.
candidates.main_reservation: The underlying CRISPR platform already received the 2020 Chemistry prize; this entry must reward hemoglobin regulation and target biology. Clinical treatment development involved additional teams.
candidates.attribution_note: Thein supplied human genetic identification; Sankaran and Orkin established repressor function; Bauer helped identify and dissect the therapeutic erythroid enhancer. Restored Thein and Bauer rather than attributing the entire chain to Orkin and Sankaran alone.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: BCR-ABL inhibition and molecularly targeted treatment of chronic myeloid leukemia
candidates.scientific_basis: Imatinib targets the BCR-ABL kinase driving CML; investigation of resistance enabled subsequent targeted inhibitors.
candidates.rationale: A durable demonstration that targeting an oncogenic driver can transform cancer treatment.
candidates.main_reservation: Broader precision-oncology claims overlap with HER2 therapy and depend on many earlier discoveries.
candidates.attribution_note: Keep this kinase-inhibitor achievement separate from trastuzumab; any combined award must still fit the total three-person limit.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: Biomolecular condensates and phase separation in cellular organization
candidates.scientific_basis: Phase separation and interactions of low-complexity protein domains explain important forms of cellular organization without membrane boundaries.
candidates.rationale: Introduced a physical mechanism for organizing cellular reactions, with experimental work from complementary approaches.
candidates.main_reservation: Some proposed functions remain contested or context-dependent; liquid behavior, hydrogels and aggregation should not be equated.
candidates.attribution_note: Hyman-Brangwynne and Gorlich-McKnight support different emphases; select a precise achievement and at most three researchers during deliberation.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Causal roles of gut microbial communities in host metabolism and childhood growth
candidates.scientific_basis: Transfer of defined or human-derived microbiota into germ-free animals separated causal metabolic effects from association; microbiota-directed food studies tested translation.
candidates.rationale: A foundational experimental route from microbiome association to causality.
candidates.main_reservation: Clinical generalization depends on disease and intervention; a broad microbiome award risks diffuse attribution.
candidates.attribution_note: Gordon led the experimental framework. Peter Turnbaugh, Laura Blanton, Tahmeed Ahmed and collaborating teams made major specific contributions; a malnutrition-treatment citation would need a wider pool than this foundational program entry.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: CFTR functional rescue and modulator therapies for cystic fibrosis
candidates.scientific_basis: Understanding CFTR dysfunction enabled drugs that improve mutant protein folding, trafficking and channel activity.
candidates.rationale: A mature example of treating a genetic disease by rescuing the defective protein mechanism.
candidates.main_reservation: The mechanistic, screening and medicinal-chemistry contributions are distributed among more than three scientists.
candidates.attribution_note: The 2025 Lasker names Welsh, Negulescu and Gonzalez; its scientific account also credits Van Goor and Hadida, retained as alternatives.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Chaperonin-assisted protein folding
candidates.subfield: Molecular cell biology and protein biochemistry
candidates.scientific_basis: Chaperonins provide a protected environment in which proteins can fold, establishing active cellular assistance to protein folding.
candidates.rationale: Changed a basic account of how functional proteins arise in cells; attribution is comparatively compact.
candidates.main_reservation: Could compete with the unfolded protein response; the committee must distinguish assisted folding from structure prediction.
candidates.attribution_note: This is experimental chaperonin biology, distinct from AlphaFold and computational protein design recognized by Chemistry in 2024.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Discovery, mapping, and cloning of BRCA1-linked inherited breast and ovarian cancer susceptibility
candidates.scientific_basis: Linkage analysis established a major inherited susceptibility locus; subsequent positional cloning identified BRCA1 and disease-associated variants.
candidates.rationale: An identifiable discovery changed disease risk assessment and preventive medicine.
candidates.main_reservation: Mapping the locus, cloning BRCA1, identifying BRCA2 and exploiting DNA-repair vulnerabilities are different achievements.
candidates.attribution_note: King established inherited susceptibility and mapped the BRCA1 locus; Skolnick’s consortium cloned the gene in 1994. They are complementary stages, not interchangeable claims of first discovery. Miki and other consortium contributors retain historical scientific credit; this pool is provisional.
candidates.review_decision: Broadened locus-mapping-only scope to include gene cloning; retained Mark H. Skolnick from Claude.

candidates.discovery: Distinct B- and T-lymphocyte lineages and their roles in adaptive immunity
candidates.scientific_basis: Thymus and bursa experiments established separate cellular and antibody-producing arms of adaptive immunity.
candidates.rationale: An organizing discovery underlying modern immunology.
candidates.main_reservation: A very old discovery with many later immunological prizes; age of the work does not invalidate it.
candidates.attribution_note: Miller established the thymus-dependent lineage; Cooper separated bursa-dependent antibody immunity from thymus-dependent cellular immunity. Do not fold the distinct T-cell receptor discovery into this entry.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: DNA methylation as a mechanism regulating gene expression
candidates.scientific_basis: DNA methylation and its recognition influence gene activity; causal experiments connect methylation changes to disease mechanisms.
candidates.rationale: A fundamental account of stable gene regulation beyond DNA sequence, supported by mechanistic experiments.
candidates.main_reservation: Different discoveries under the broad epigenetics label should not be treated as a single undifferentiated achievement.
candidates.attribution_note: Bird and Cedar anchor methylation and expression; Jaenisch represents causal mammalian experiments. Imprinting remains a separate candidate.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Rudolf Jaenisch for causal methylation experiments alongside Bird and Cedar. Kept disease-specific MECP2/Rett separately, with overlap flagged.

candidates.discovery: Fetal cell-free DNA in maternal blood and noninvasive prenatal screening
candidates.scientific_basis: Cell-free fetal DNA detection in maternal plasma enabled blood-based screening for fetal chromosomal abnormalities.
candidates.rationale: A specific diagnostic discovery with widespread clinical translation.
candidates.main_reservation: Screening and definitive diagnosis are different; any broader sequencing/algorithm citation requires additional attribution.
candidates.attribution_note: Lo drove the fetal plasma-DNA discovery and translation. Preserve the focused citation rather than assigning all liquid biopsy discoveries to him.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Genetically engineered CAR-T cells for treating cancer
candidates.scientific_basis: Engineering T-cell receptors and signaling enabled patient T cells to attack blood cancers, with durable remissions in some patients.
candidates.rationale: A mature clinical transformation built on a distinct engineering advance, with an intelligible two-person configuration.
candidates.main_reservation: Durability, toxicities and limited solid-tumor success constrain generalization; earlier invention credit must be acknowledged.
candidates.attribution_note: June and Sadelain supply receptor engineering and clinical translation; Rosenberg’s NCI program also contributed early clinical CAR-T work, so retain Claude’s addition. Do not attribute CAR engineering to Rosenberg merely from TIL therapy; Kochenderfer and other clinical pioneers remain relevant for a broader citation. Eshhar’s original engineering contribution remains historical credit.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Steven A. Rosenberg from Claude with an explicit CAR-T contribution boundary.

candidates.discovery: GLP-1 physiology and the development of incretin therapies for diabetes and obesity
candidates.scientific_basis: Discovery of active GLP-1 and its insulin-stimulating physiology enabled development of durable therapeutic analogues.
candidates.rationale: Combines a defined physiological discovery with major demonstrated clinical benefit; the scientific and therapeutic narratives both support consideration.
candidates.main_reservation: Four substantial living attribution claims compete for at most three laureate places; citation scope could determine the outcome.
candidates.attribution_note: Retain Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen. Discovery-focused and drug-development-focused configurations differ. Habener is indispensable historical credit but died on 28 December 2025 and is removed from the eligible pool.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: HER2-directed antibody therapy for breast cancer
candidates.scientific_basis: HER2 biology, antibody engineering and clinical development produced trastuzumab for HER2-positive breast cancer.
candidates.rationale: A mature, specific route from molecular disease classification to survival-improving treatment.
candidates.main_reservation: A combined targeted-cancer-therapy citation would create severe competition for laureate places.
candidates.attribution_note: Keep the HER2 antibody development pool intact and separate from the BCR-ABL kinase-inhibitor pool.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: High-frequency deep brain stimulation for Parkinson’s disease
candidates.scientific_basis: High-frequency stimulation provided a reversible alternative to lesioning, with the subthalamic nucleus becoming a major therapeutic target.
candidates.rationale: A transformative intervention grounded in neural-circuit physiology.
candidates.main_reservation: Award credit includes deceased circuit pioneer Mahlon DeLong and clinical collaborators; symptom control is not disease modification.
candidates.attribution_note: Benabid established the stimulation intervention; DeLong identified relevant circuit pathology and target rationale. DeLong is historical credit only. Pierre Pollak and other clinical pioneers are relevant to a broader translational citation.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

historical_contributors.name: Mahlon R. DeLong
historical_contributors.contribution: Basal-ganglia circuit model and subthalamic target rationale

candidates.discovery: Identification of CFTR as the gene responsible for cystic fibrosis
candidates.scientific_basis: Positional cloning and characterization identified CFTR and connected its disruption to cystic fibrosis.
candidates.rationale: A landmark demonstration of finding a disease gene from inheritance and chromosome position.
candidates.main_reservation: The original gene discovery and later functional rescue therapies offer competing citation scopes.
candidates.attribution_note: Keep gene discovery separate from the Welsh-Negulescu-Gonzalez therapeutic candidate; do not conflate source credit with drug-development credit.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: IL-6 signaling and therapeutic blockade of the IL-6 receptor
candidates.scientific_basis: Discovery and characterization of IL-6 and its signaling system enabled receptor-blocking treatment such as tocilizumab.
candidates.rationale: A coherent molecular-to-clinical story with complementary mechanistic contributions and established treatment relevance.
candidates.main_reservation: A broad cytokine-therapy award risks conflating this discovery with anti-TNF or IL-1 biology.
candidates.attribution_note: The 2011 Japan Prize supports this two-person pool; retain a distinct IL-6 citation.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Integrins as receptors mediating cell-matrix and cell-cell adhesion
candidates.scientific_basis: Separate discoveries of extracellular matrix and leukocyte adhesion receptors converged on the integrin family.
candidates.rationale: A general organizing principle of tissues and immunity with mature evidence and a coherent three-person configuration.
candidates.main_reservation: The field is broad; an award needs a sharply defined receptor discovery rather than a general adhesion citation.
candidates.attribution_note: Retain both extracellular matrix and immune adhesion origins when evaluating the common molecular family.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Kinetic stabilization of transthyretin and treatment of amyloid disease
candidates.scientific_basis: Stabilizing the transthyretin tetramer with tafamidis reduces its dissociation and aggregation and slows disease progression.
candidates.rationale: A precise, experimentally grounded connection between protein mechanism and effective disease-modifying therapy.
candidates.main_reservation: A narrow disease-focused achievement may compete with broader proteostasis principles; drug-development attribution needs scrutiny.
candidates.attribution_note: Kelly anchors the mechanism-and-therapy discovery; avoid claiming that tafamidis demonstrates a universal treatment for all amyloid diseases.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Leptin and endocrine regulation of appetite and body weight
candidates.scientific_basis: Identification of leptin established an endocrine signal linking adipose tissue to feeding behavior and body-weight regulation.
candidates.rationale: A fundamental physiological discovery that changed the biological understanding of obesity.
candidates.main_reservation: The clinical replacement-therapy story is narrower than that for incretin drugs; this is a distinct mechanism, not a GLP-1 variant.
candidates.attribution_note: Friedman is the living pool for this discovery-centered entry; Coleman is indispensable historical credit but died in 2014.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

historical_contributors.name: Douglas L. Coleman
historical_contributors.contribution: Genetic and physiological prediction of the leptin pathway

candidates.discovery: Long-term potentiation and the synaptic basis of learning and memory
candidates.scientific_basis: Experiments linked persistent strengthening of hippocampal synapses and its molecular mechanisms to spatial learning and memory.
candidates.rationale: Combines fundamental physiology with causal investigation of a central brain function.
candidates.main_reservation: A new citation must make clear its distinction from earlier Nobel-recognized work on memory and from place-cell discoveries.
candidates.attribution_note: Bliss and Lømo established LTP experimentally; Collingridge elucidated NMDA-dependent mechanisms; Morris linked synaptic plasticity to spatial learning. Retain all four as alternative roles instead of dropping either Lømo or Collingridge to force a trio.
candidates.review_decision: United complementary discovery, mechanism and memory contributions; retained Terje Lømo and Graham L. Collingridge.

candidates.discovery: Mammalian genomic imprinting and parent-of-origin gene expression
candidates.scientific_basis: Independent embryo experiments established functional nonequivalence of maternal and paternal genomes and the basis of genomic imprinting.
candidates.rationale: An unexpected, fundamental discovery with direct consequences for development and human genetic disorders.
candidates.main_reservation: Its relation to DNA methylation can invite overbroad merging; the original developmental discovery should remain identifiable.
candidates.attribution_note: Keep the independent Surani and Solter discoveries together, while distinguishing later molecular imprint maintenance mechanisms.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: Massively parallel DNA sequencing for genome-scale biology and medicine
candidates.scientific_basis: Scalable massively parallel sequencing made DNA sequence analysis broadly usable in biomedical research and medicine.
candidates.rationale: An enabling invention with exceptional effects on genetics, diagnostics and experimental biology.
candidates.main_reservation: The invention is also a plausible Chemistry achievement; alternative sequencing platforms have separate priority histories.
candidates.attribution_note: This is the specific pool recognized by the 2022 Breakthrough Prize. Do not conflate it with every next-generation or long-read sequencing platform.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: MECP2 biology, the molecular cause of Rett syndrome, and reversibility in mouse models
candidates.scientific_basis: MECP2 mutation discovery connected a methylated-DNA binding protein to Rett syndrome; gene restoration reversed established phenotypes in mice.
candidates.rationale: A molecular explanation of a neurological syndrome with a striking proof of reversibility.
candidates.main_reservation: Clinical reversal is not established by the mouse rescue result; overlap with the general DNA methylation entry requires citation discipline.
candidates.attribution_note: Zoghbi’s team, including Ruthie Amir, identified disease mutations. Bird’s team discovered MeCP2 biology and demonstrated mouse rescue. Broadened the title so it does not incorrectly attribute the mutation-discovery experiment to Bird.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Mitochondrial DNA inheritance and mutations as causes of human disease
candidates.scientific_basis: Maternal mitochondrial inheritance and pathogenic mtDNA mutations established a distinct genetic basis for metabolic and degenerative disease.
candidates.rationale: A foundational human-genetic framework outside nuclear Mendelian inheritance.
candidates.main_reservation: Pathogenic deletions and mutations were identified by multiple groups; narrowing the citation matters.
candidates.attribution_note: Focus Wallace’s entry on mitochondrial inheritance/disease. Removed the generic human-evolution claim from the title so the committee can assess a specific medical achievement; Ian Holt, Anita Harding and other pioneers remain relevant historical attribution.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Modern multichannel cochlear implants and speech-processing strategies
candidates.scientific_basis: Multichannel stimulation and improved encoding strategies made meaningful speech recognition possible in profound deafness.
candidates.rationale: A durable medical invention restoring access to an impaired sensory function.
candidates.main_reservation: Scientific scope should focus on the modern implant rather than the first electrical hearing experiment.
candidates.attribution_note: Clark and Hochmair developed multichannel devices; Wilson developed effective signal processing. Erwin Hochmair and earlier pioneers remain relevant credit; this pool follows the scoped modern-implant scientific account.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Molecular identification and cloning of the T-cell antigen receptor
candidates.scientific_basis: Independent mouse and human T-cell cDNA cloning programs identified rearranging antigen-receptor genes in 1984.
candidates.rationale: A foundational molecular explanation of antigen recognition by T cells.
candidates.main_reservation: A wider citation covering protein identification would require additional attribution beyond the cloning programs.
candidates.attribution_note: Davis and Mak led independent programs; Hedrick and Yanagi were first authors of the original mouse and human cloning papers. Their inclusion is provisional scientific credit, not an inference that first authors automatically deserve a Nobel. Earlier protein identification by Reinherz, Marrack and Kappler is outside this narrowed citation.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Molecular mechanisms of bacterial quorum sensing and coordinated behavior
candidates.scientific_basis: Diffusible signals and cognate receptors allow bacteria to coordinate gene expression according to population context.
candidates.rationale: A fundamental change in understanding microbial collective behavior with infection relevance.
candidates.main_reservation: Award scope must distinguish molecular mechanism from the first observations of bacterial communication; established therapeutic impact is more limited.
candidates.attribution_note: Bassler and Greenberg elucidated interspecies and species-specific signaling systems and their biological implications. Earlier observations and genetic work by Hastings, Nealson, Silverman and others predate this contribution; avoid claiming these two alone first observed communication.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Neural and computational mechanisms linking reward prediction errors to learning
candidates.scientific_basis: Dopamine recordings, computational reinforcement-learning models and human neuroimaging linked predicted rewards and outcomes to learning.
candidates.rationale: A major connection between neural activity, computation and behavior.
candidates.main_reservation: The broad learning citation differs from the narrower claim that one scientist discovered all dopamine prediction-error signaling.
candidates.attribution_note: Schultz supplies neurophysiology; Dayan and Montague supply computational links; Dolan supplies human decision/reward evidence. The 1997 synthesis is coauthored by Schultz, Dayan and Montague. Broadened Claude’s title to match its inclusion of Dolan.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Notch signaling as a mechanism of cell-fate specification
candidates.scientific_basis: Genetic and molecular discoveries established how Notch signaling controls cell fate, development and tissue patterning.
candidates.rationale: A conserved biological mechanism with foundational experimental support and continuing relevance to tissue biology.
candidates.main_reservation: Cell-fate specification has many historical contributors, and the precise discovery boundary matters.
candidates.attribution_note: These are the three researchers jointly recognized by Gairdner in 2025; this pool is a defensible starting point rather than exhaustive historical credit.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Optical coherence tomography for noninvasive tissue imaging
candidates.scientific_basis: Optical coherence tomography produces depth-resolved cross-sectional images of tissue and transformed retinal examination.
candidates.rationale: A mature invention with extensive direct medical use and a compact attribution configuration.
candidates.main_reservation: Its optics foundation could also support consideration in Physics; Medicine requires a convincing clinical-invention framing.
candidates.attribution_note: Use the imaging-invention trio; keep OCT distinct from the separate VEGF discovery even though both transformed retinal care.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Optogenetic control of genetically specified cells with light
candidates.scientific_basis: Light-sensitive microbial proteins and genetic targeting permit experimental activation or inhibition of specified neuronal populations.
candidates.rationale: Enabled causal experiments on neural circuits at a scale and specificity that changed neuroscience.
candidates.main_reservation: Several independent enabling contributions make a three-person award difficult; tool impact and biological discovery need to be distinguished.
candidates.attribution_note: Preserve the six living researchers named by the 2013 Brain Prize. Oesterhelt is historical credit only because he died in 2022.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Georg Nagel and the other five opsin/optogenetics pioneers; names remain an alternative pool rather than a six-person award recommendation.

candidates.discovery: Orexin/hypocretin discovery and its role in wakefulness and narcolepsy
candidates.scientific_basis: Orexin signaling maintains wakefulness, and loss of this system explains narcolepsy; the pathway also supplies drug targets.
candidates.rationale: Connects a basic physiological discovery to a defined human disorder and pharmacology, with clear complementary attribution.
candidates.main_reservation: Therapeutic maturity differs between receptor antagonism for insomnia and receptor agonism for narcolepsy.
candidates.attribution_note: Yanagisawa and Sakurai identified orexins/receptors; de Lecea and Kilduff independently identified hypocretins in Sutcliffe’s program. Mignot linked receptor defects and human peptide deficiency to narcolepsy; Yanagisawa’s knockout work connected the system to sleep. A narcolepsy-centered citation and a peptide-discovery citation imply different recipient selections.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Sakurai from Claude and restored the independent hypocretin discovery team to the broader scope.

candidates.discovery: PCSK9 and human genetic validation of a cholesterol-lowering therapeutic target
candidates.scientific_basis: PCSK9 disease mutations and protective loss-of-function variants established a target for reducing LDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk.
candidates.rationale: A strong example of human genetics directing therapeutic development, with clear physiological consequences.
candidates.main_reservation: Several discovery and validation teams compete for the three-person limit; distinction from earlier LDL-receptor recognition is necessary.
candidates.attribution_note: Retain protein discovery, disease genetics and protective-variant teams; a Hobbs-Cohen-only framing would prematurely exclude foundational work.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Marianne Abifadel for disease-causing PCSK9 mutation discovery; distinguished this from Seidah protein biology and Hobbs/Cohen protective human genetics.

candidates.discovery: Perivascular cerebrospinal-fluid exchange and the proposed glymphatic clearance mechanism
candidates.scientific_basis: In-vivo tracer experiments described astroglial/perivascular routes for CSF exchange and solute removal, followed by sleep and human studies.
candidates.rationale: A potentially important physiological framework for brain-fluid homeostasis.
candidates.main_reservation: Transport interpretation and the effects of sleep remain contested; 2024 contrary mouse clearance results and 2026 supportive human evidence use different methods and do not by themselves settle the dispute.
candidates.attribution_note: Iliff led the original experimental report in Nedergaard’s program and is added. Keep this discovery for independent assessment, while treating the complete clearance model as a hypothesis under active testing.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Sarcomere gene mutations as causes of inherited hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
candidates.scientific_basis: Familial disease mapping and mutation identification established inherited sarcomere defects as causes of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
candidates.rationale: A disease-defining genetic mechanism that changed diagnosis and mechanistic treatment research.
candidates.main_reservation: A specific genetic disease package rather than a single universal cardiovascular mechanism.
candidates.attribution_note: Retain the Seidmans for their joint clinical-genetic and experimental program; do not credit them with inventing every subsequent myosin-directed drug.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: Spatial transcriptomics for mapping gene expression within intact tissue
candidates.scientific_basis: Spatially resolved sequencing and multiplexed RNA imaging associate molecular cell identity with tissue position.
candidates.rationale: Restores anatomical context to molecular cell analysis and enables detailed investigation of tissue organization.
candidates.main_reservation: Distinct sequencing and imaging inventions have separate priorities, and application maturity varies.
candidates.attribution_note: Zhuang anchors MERFISH; Lundeberg, Frisen and Stahl anchor the spatial sequencing approach. Linnarsson coauthored the original spatial-transcriptomics paper.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: Tau and alpha-synuclein as molecular components of pathological neurodegenerative filaments
candidates.scientific_basis: Tau was identified in Alzheimer filaments and alpha-synuclein in Lewy pathology, defining molecularly distinct proteinopathies.
candidates.rationale: Molecular characterization reshaped disease classification and mechanism research.
candidates.main_reservation: Tau and synuclein are distinct achievements within one thematic entry; selecting a citation may require narrowing the protein and attribution.
candidates.attribution_note: Goedert’s program established tau filament biology; Spillantini and Goedert colleagues identified alpha-synuclein in Lewy bodies. Contributions by Virginia Lee, Claude Wischik, Ross Jakes and other pioneers are not erased; this pool is provisional, not exhaustive.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: TGF-beta receptor-to-SMAD signaling and its control of cell fate
candidates.scientific_basis: Receptor and downstream transcriptional mechanisms explain how TGF-beta regulates proliferation and cell identity in context.
candidates.rationale: A major mechanism connecting extracellular cues to developmental and disease programs.
candidates.main_reservation: Many groups contributed receptors and SMAD biology; a single-person pool cannot settle the entire field’s priority.
candidates.attribution_note: Scope is Massagué’s mechanistic signaling program, not initial isolation of TGF-beta. Rik Derynck, Kohei Miyazono and other receptor/SMAD pioneers are relevant if agents choose a pathway-wide citation.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

candidates.discovery: The cGAS-STING pathway linking cytosolic DNA sensing to innate immunity
candidates.scientific_basis: STING is an innate immune signaling adaptor; cGAS detects cytosolic DNA and produces the cyclic messenger cGAMP.
candidates.rationale: A clearly defined mechanism with consequences for infection, inflammation and antitumor immunity.
candidates.main_reservation: The clinical translational story is less mature than the mechanistic discovery, and a broad citation complicates credit.
candidates.attribution_note: Barber and Ishikawa identified STING; Chen’s laboratory, including Sun and Wu, identified cGAS and cGAMP signaling. Preserve first-author experimental contributions explicitly. A cGAS-only citation and a full cGAS–STING citation are different award packages.
candidates.review_decision: Retained the broader supported pool; normalized Zhijian J. Chen to Zhijian James Chen.

candidates.discovery: The nuclear hormone receptor superfamily and ligand-dependent gene regulation
candidates.scientific_basis: Receptor gene cloning exposed a related family of ligand-regulated transcription factors, followed by orphan-receptor and RXR biology.
candidates.rationale: A unifying mechanism across endocrine, metabolic and developmental physiology.
candidates.main_reservation: Foundational credit also belongs to deceased pioneers; a one-person living pool must not imply a one-person discovery.
candidates.attribution_note: Evans contributed receptor cloning and the superfamily/orphan-receptor program. Jensen established earlier hormone-receptor biology and Chambon made parallel molecular discoveries; both remain historical credit. The current pool is not exhaustive of living contributors such as receptor/coregulator specialists.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

historical_contributors.name: Pierre Chambon
historical_contributors.contribution: Parallel nuclear receptor cloning and mechanism

historical_contributors.name: Elwood V. Jensen
historical_contributors.contribution: Hormone receptor discovery and gene-regulation framework

candidates.discovery: The unfolded protein response and signaling from the endoplasmic reticulum
candidates.scientific_basis: Identification of ER stress signaling machinery explained how cells sense misfolded proteins and increase their folding capacity.
candidates.rationale: A fundamental, widely reproduced cellular mechanism with an unusually clear two-person attribution.
candidates.main_reservation: Direct therapeutic benefit is less prominent than its biological importance; related proteostasis discoveries are separate candidates.
candidates.attribution_note: Keep ER stress sensing and signaling separate from chaperonin-assisted folding and from therapeutic stabilization of transthyretin.
candidates.review_decision: Retained discovery and supported provisional attribution pool from the Codex draft.

candidates.discovery: TNF blockade as a treatment for rheumatoid arthritis and inflammatory disease
candidates.scientific_basis: Experimental work identified TNF as an actionable inflammatory driver and clinical studies established effective TNF blockade.
candidates.rationale: A compelling mechanism-to-treatment story with established benefit and clear complementary laboratory and clinical roles.
candidates.main_reservation: The previous Medicine prize addressed immune tolerance; thematic succession is a forecasting consideration, not an exclusion rule.
candidates.attribution_note: Retain this cytokine-blockade discovery independently of IL-6 and the already rewarded regulatory T-cell story.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: TOR signaling as a regulator of cell growth and nutrient responses
candidates.scientific_basis: TOR proteins couple nutrient availability to cell growth; mammalian TOR signaling extends this mechanism to physiological regulation.
candidates.rationale: A central conserved mechanism with effects across metabolism, growth and disease.
candidates.main_reservation: Discovery of yeast TOR, mammalian mTOR and later pathway mechanisms support different attribution boundaries.
candidates.attribution_note: Hall identified yeast TOR and nutrient-growth regulation; Schreiber supplied rapamycin-target chemical biology; Sabatini identified mammalian RAFT1/mTOR. The original 1994 paper supports retaining Sabatini; omission from one draft is not evidence of scientific ineligibility.
candidates.review_decision: Retained David M. Sabatini with an original-paper basis for mammalian TOR credit.

candidates.discovery: VEGF biology and inhibition of pathological angiogenesis
candidates.scientific_basis: VEGF and vascular permeability factor proved to be the same signaling molecule; blocking VEGF enabled anti-angiogenic treatment.
candidates.rationale: Connects a defined biological pathway to mature clinical benefit, particularly in retinal disease.
candidates.main_reservation: Discovery of permeability activity, molecular identification and therapeutic development support different credit allocations.
candidates.attribution_note: Ferrara is central to a therapeutic citation; Dvorak and Senger become important for a broader discovery-of-VEGF/VPF citation.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Senger and Dvorak for early VPF discovery and Ferrara for VEGF molecular/therapeutic work; the clinical citation may favor a narrower pool.

candidates.discovery: Virus-like particle vaccines that prevent HPV infection and related cancers
candidates.scientific_basis: Noninfectious papillomavirus-like particles can induce protective immunity and form the basis of vaccines preventing HPV infection.
candidates.rationale: Links a precise technological advance to cancer prevention and substantial public-health benefit.
candidates.main_reservation: Particle design, immunogenicity and vaccine development have overlapping priority histories.
candidates.attribution_note: Retain Lowy, Schiller and Frazer for committee attribution review; the Lasker account describes both the NCI work and Frazer contribution.
candidates.review_decision: Merged the shared discovery; retained both drafts’ supported names, including Claude’s other_names, without selecting a preferred trio.

candidates.discovery: Wnt genes and signaling in cell fate, development, and tissue renewal
candidates.scientific_basis: int-1/Wnt1 identification connected an oncogenic integration site to a conserved developmental signaling family.
candidates.rationale: A broad organizing pathway linking development, stem cells and disease.
candidates.main_reservation: Varmus is already a 1989 Medicine laureate; any new citation must establish a distinct achievement rather than re-award the cellular-oncogene discovery.
candidates.attribution_note: Nusse and Varmus jointly identified int-1/Wnt1; Nusse extended the developmental and stem-cell signaling program. Add Varmus as scientific credit while explicitly flagging prior-award overlap; prior laureates are not automatically barred from distinct awards.
candidates.review_decision: Retained Claude-only discovery after reviewing scientific scope and attribution.

prior_award_flags.issue: A new Wnt citation must be distinguished from the already rewarded cellular origin of retroviral oncogenes.
